author: TeIq
content:
## Source
.design/m5/43-federation.md — All ACs (AC-1 through AC-8) + decomposition PR 6.

## Surface
- New test: `polaris-backend/tests/federation_two_instance_e2e.rs` — spins up two `polaris-backend` instances under `testcontainers`, with separate Postgres DBs and separate MockFetcher PDS fixtures. Exercises the full federation handshake.

## Test plan
1. Boot instance A with `[[federation_peers]] did = "<B-DID>" direction = "bidirectional"`.
2. Boot instance B with `[[federation_peers]] did = "<A-DID>" direction = "bidirectional"`.
3. A's MockFetcher hosts B's PDS repo (so A can subscribe to B's firehose).
4. AC-1: A publishes a `polaris.escalation` referencing an incident, naming B. Within 10s, B materializes it in `federation_escalations`.
5. AC-2: B posts a reply via `polaris.escalation-message`; A's case view shows it attributed to `instance:<B-DID>`.
6. AC-3: Boot an instance C not listed in A's peers. C publishes a `polaris.escalation` targeting A. A receives it but lands it in `federation_quarantine`, not `federation_escalations`.
7. AC-4: Inspect every wire record written by A; assert none contains a moderator ID (search the serialized JSON).
8. AC-5: A labels subject X as `harassment`; B labels X as `not-harmful`. Both labels persist on both sides as `ExternalLabel` observations.
9. AC-6: A sends a `polaris.escalation-message` to B with a tampered signature. B logs WARN, does NOT insert into `federation_messages`.
10. AC-7: Drop the WebSocket between A and B mid-Active state; reconnect; verify both sides resume at last-known-good state.
11. AC-8: `polaris federation-status` on A lists the escalation with all required fields.

## Rust-quality notes
- **Use `testcontainers` for both Postgres instances** (already a workspace pattern, see `polaris-backend/tests/threats_common/mod.rs`).
- **MockFetcher reuse** — the same MockFetcher pattern v1 uses (`polaris-backend/tests/setup_endpoints.rs`) hosts the peer's PDS responses.
- Wall-clock budget: <60s. Each AC step has a `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), …)` so a stalled federation never hangs the test suite (per rust-quality §10 — no infinite waits in tests).
- Per rust-quality §7: this is one integration test exercising all 8 ACs; do NOT split into 8 tests — the setup cost (two backends + two DBs + two MockFetchers) is high. One test with a fixture function `fn two_instance_fixture() -> (Backend, Backend) { … }` and 8 numbered AC blocks inside the body.
- Per rust-quality §10 (async gotchas): never hold `std::sync::MutexGuard` across `.await`. Use `tokio::sync::Mutex` for any state shared between the two backends in-test.

## External references
- testcontainers Postgres: https://docs.rs/testcontainers-modules/latest/testcontainers_modules/postgres/index.html
- Existing two-process test pattern (reference): `polaris-backend/tests/setup_endpoints.rs`
- `tokio::time::timeout`: https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/time/fn.timeout.html

## Acceptance
- [ ] All eight ACs covered by named blocks in the test body.
- [ ] CI runs in <60s wall-clock.
- [ ] Failing any AC produces a diff-style error pointing at the broken step.
